title: Automated Emergency Dispatch Coordination
business: Emergency medical dispatch centers managing high-volume, time-sensitive triage calls.
problem: Dispatchers struggle to maintain situational awareness while simultaneously querying multiple internal databases to verify patient history and resource availability, leading to cognitive overload and potential delays in critical information retrieval.
solution: By utilizing the gpt-realtime-2 model, dispatch centers can deploy a voice-agent that uses its reasoning capabilities to interpret complex, non-linear emergency descriptions while concurrently executing tool calls to retrieve patient records and dispatch units in real-time.
steps: Configure the gpt-realtime-2 session via the v1/realtime endpoint to enable bi-directional audio streaming.
Define specific function calling schemas for the agent to query external patient databases and unit availability systems.
Set the reasoning effort parameter to balance the need for deep analytical processing of emergency symptoms against the requirement for low-latency voice responses.
Implement the realtime event loop to handle incoming audio streams and outgoing tool call requests.
Monitor the reasoning token usage to ensure the agent maintains a fluid, conversational pace during high-stress triage scenarios.
outcome: The system achieves a more cohesive triage process where the agent acts as a cognitive assistant, allowing human dispatchers to focus on high-level decision-making while the model handles the technical retrieval and synthesis of data.
limitation: A primary trade-off is the latency introduced by higher reasoning effort settings; developers should monitor the time-to-first-token and total response duration to ensure the conversational flow remains acceptable for emergency contexts.
